## Global Aesthetic Options
```{r}
library(sf)
library(arcgis)
library(mapview)
library(janitor)
library(tidyverse)
library(sysfonts)
library(showtext)

# colors 
soe_colors <- c(
  red    = "#DD5A54",
  blush  = "#EDBFB2",
  orange = "#EC940C",
  blue   = "#608ED8",
  olive  = "#737F2E",
  forest = "#283523"
)
soe_palette <- unname(soe_colors)

## add fonts
font_add_google("Fraunces", "Fraunces")
font_add_google("Manrope", "Manrope")
showtext_auto()
showtext_opts(dpi = 300)

# ggplot theme
theme_soe <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Manrope") +
    theme(
      text             = element_text(color = soe_colors["forest"]),
      plot.title       = element_text(family = "Fraunces", face = "bold",
                                      size = rel(1.4)),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(face = "italic", size = rel(1.1)),
      axis.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position  = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.border     = element_rect(color = soe_colors["forest"],
                                      fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
      strip.background = element_rect(color = soe_colors["forest"],
                                      fill = NA, linewidth = 0.6),
      strip.text       = element_text(family = "Fraunces", face = "bold",
                                      color = soe_colors["forest"])
    )
}
theme_set(theme_soe())

# create discrete and continuous palettes
options(
  ggplot2.discrete.colour = list(soe_palette),
  ggplot2.discrete.fill   = list(soe_palette),
  # continuous scales: blush -> red
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = function(...) scale_colour_gradient(
    low = soe_colors["blush"], high = soe_colors["red"], ...),
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = function(...) scale_fill_gradient(
    low = soe_colors["blush"], high = soe_colors["red"], ...)
)
```


## Read and tidy data 
```{r}
setwd("~/Google Drive/My Drive/Teaching/ES-314/Class Research/data")

nri <- read_csv("NRI/NRI_Table_CensusTracts.csv") |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  filter(stateabbrv %in% c("MA", "CT", "ME", "NH", "RI", "VT")) |> 
  select(tractfips, county, stateabbrv, risk_value, hwav_riskv, hrcn_riskv) |> 
  mutate(
    risk_pct_rank = percent_rank(risk_value) * 100,
    hwav_pct_rank = cume_dist(hwav_riskv) * 100,
    hrcn_pct_rank = cume_dist(hrcn_riskv) * 100)
```


## 1. Average NRI scores
Calculate average percentile rank risk score for Norfolk, and MA
```{r}
# MA- 48th percentile in NE
nri |> filter(stateabbrv == "MA") |> select(risk_pct_rank) |> summary()


# Norfolk County - 60th percentile in NE
nri |> filter(stateabbrv == "MA" & county == "Norfolk") |> select(risk_pct_rank) |> summary()
```

## 4. Combined Bar graph
```{r}
score_cols <- c("risk_pct_rank", "hwav_pct_rank", "hrcn_pct_rank")

# state scores
by_state <- nri |>
  group_by(stateabbrv) |>
  summarise(
    across(all_of(score_cols), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(geography = if_else(stateabbrv == "MA", "Massachusetts", "EPA Region 1"))

# county scores
by_county <- nri |>
  filter(stateabbrv == "MA", county == "Norfolk") |>
  group_by(stateabbrv) |> 
  summarise(
    across(all_of(score_cols), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  mutate(geography = "Norfolk County")

# df for creating bar chart 
bar_df <- bind_rows(by_state, by_county) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(risk_pct_rank, hwav_pct_rank, hrcn_pct_rank),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "avg_pct_rank") |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("risk_pct_rank", "hwav_pct_rank", "hrcn_pct_rank"),
      labels = c("Average Risk", "Average Heat Wave", "Average Hurricane")),
    facet = factor(
      geography,
      levels = c("EPA Region 1", "Massachusetts", "Norfolk County"))) |> 
filter(!(facet == "EPA Region 1" & stateabbrv == "MA")) |> 
   mutate(stateabbrv = ifelse(stateabbrv == "MA", " ", stateabbrv))

ggplot(bar_df, aes(x = stateabbrv, y = avg_pct_rank, fill = metric)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(avg_pct_rank)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_grid(~ facet, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average percentile rank",
    fill = NULL
  ) + 
  theme(legend.position = "right")

rm(nri, by_county, by_state, bar_df, score_cols)
```


## 5. Map of Avg Projected Heat by cities/towns + county over it ? 
https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-026-06909-w [heat stress data from the past, HUGE files]
https://share-open-data-metroboston.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/6f2c0c8e89f541a8bd8e5611da058bea_0/explore 

[NASA data](https://www.earthdata.nasa.gov/data/catalog/sedac-ciesin-sedac-crv-uscrpc-2040-2049-1.00#overview), extreme heat is defined as number of events exceeding the 97.5th percentile of daily maximum baseline temperature for three consecutive days in the 2040s. 

Note that I can't find a great downscaled raster for projected extreme data. 
One option is to use the county level projections from NASA, overlay towns 
and counties [read more here](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/massgis-data-2020-us-census-towns), 
and then add an inset for Norfolk. 
```{r}
setwd("~/Google Drive/My Drive/Teaching/ES-314/Class Research/data") 

clim_risk <- st_read("US_CRP_2040-2049/Shapefile/crv-us-climate-risk-proj-county-2040-2049.shp")

clim_risk |> 
  mutate(state = substring(GEOID, 1, 2)) |> 
  filter(state == 25) |> 
  mapview(zcol = "HeatExt")

```
